messages:
PagerDuty Bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (us-east-1). 5xx% 12.3 -> paging SRE Oncall :rotating_light:
SRE Oncall: I'm on it, looking at dashboard now. which routes are spiking?
Runtime Eng: batcher_v2 queue depth up, head-of-line lag increasing. lots of queued small requests piling behind long-running big prompts.
Matt O.: seeing gateway timeouts from api-gw -> inference-gateway, 504s rising. region: us-east-1 (primary).
Lia K.: customer-impact: multiple sessions from acme-inc and beta users returning 504/502. CS is getting tickets.
SRE Oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) open emergency spillover to us-west-2, 2) reduce max_batch_size to 64 on batcher_v2, 3) enable aggressive eviction for stuck batches. executing now.
Runtime Eng: rolling config: ``curl -XPOST https://ops-api/configs/batcher_v2/reload -d '{"max_batch_size":64,"eviction_policy":"preemptive"}'``
PagerDuty Bot: ACTION: runbook step 2 invoked by SRE Oncall.
Matt O.: applied config, seeing batcher worker count auto-scale trigger (+3 pods). queue depth dropping slightly. latency p50 still up.
Lia K.: deploying a temporary routing rule to send low-latency customers to smaller-quantized model variant to avoid HOL blocking. patch: ``route_policy.add_rule({"priority":80,"match":"customer_tag:low_latency","target":"model-small-quant"})``
Runtime Eng: logs showing repeated stalled batches due to one request that never completes: ``worker-17 | stuck on kv-cache fetch | prompt_len=120k``. kicking evictions for >60s.
Ops Lead: did we see any node OOMs?
SRE Oncall: no OOM, just long-running CPU on tokenizer and network stall to KV store. evicted 6 batches, backlog halved. 5xx rate trending down from 12% -> 4.5%.
Customer Success: notifying ACME support channel: "We're seeing elevated errors and routed affected sessions to backup region; investigating; will follow up."
Matt O.: temporary mitigation looks effective. still seeing intermittent 502s for a subset of requests that hit large-batch paths.
Runtime Eng: next action: patch scheduler to reject single-request batches with huge prompt tokens (prompt_len > 50k) with 429 and guidance to client to stream. rolling canary now.
SRE Oncall: oncall -> Lia K. handing off active incident in 15m. Lia please ack and continue mitigation / customer comms.
Lia K.: ack. will keep spillover open and monitor. creating incident channel #inc-2319876543 for postmortem notes.
PagerDuty Bot: HANDOFF: SRE Oncall assigned to Lia K. (handoff_ts=2319876705)
Ops Lead: collect list of impacted customers + sample trace ids for postmortem. Matt, can you grab 10 traces?
Matt O.: grabbing traces now. sample ids: trace-9a2b, trace-9a2c, trace-9b0f, trace-9c90... (pushed to incident doc).
Customer Success: logging customer reports and ETA messages. queued priority replies to ACME and two other accounts.
SRE Oncall: recording immediate root cause hypothesis: scheduler batcher allowed huge single-request prompts to create long-running batches; head-of-line inhibited small requests -> queue saturation -> gateway timeouts.
Lia K.: mitigation status @5m since handoff: 5xx down to 2.1%, p99 latency improved 30%. keeping spillover for 30m, will start draining and normalizing routing if stable.
Runtime Eng: follow-ups: - permanent scheduler guardrail to cap request token length at edge - add metrics for per-request batch-time - improve KV store timeouts and retry; owner: Runtime Eng (carol).
Ops Lead: assign PM and postmortem owner. Lia -> PM?
Lia K.: accepted postmortem ownership. creating sev-inc doc and timeline.
SRE Oncall: closing active page. Lia please escalate if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
PagerDuty Bot: RESOLVE: Incident transitioned to owner Lia K. (resolve_ts=2319876820)
